subject: FastStore Q4 surge: proposal for commit conversion + throttle guard
messages:
From: Ari Shah <ari@faststore.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Unexpected Q4 spike — need short-term commit options

Hi Laura,

Hope you're well. We just pushed a marketing campaign and are seeing a sharp usage spike for the hosted text-generation endpoint — estimates suggest a 3x increase in monthly tokens for Dec. Our current hosted plan will blow past the soft limits and we want to avoid throttling for user-facing features.

Two asks: can Redwood provide (1) a short-term commit uplift (Dec and Jan) we can convert into a longer-term step-up if the traffic persists, and (2) an operational throttle guard so excess tokens are queued or routed to a cheaper variant rather than failing?

We need pricing and a timeline today if possible — legal is standing by to review any addendums. Attaching the rough usage export from our analytics.

Thanks,
Ari Shah
Head of Platform
FastStore

Attachment: faststore_usage_export_Nov2026.csv (type: text/csv)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Ari Shah <ari@faststore.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@faststore.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T11:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Q4 spike — need short-term commit options

Hi Ari + Priya — thanks for the heads up and the export. Good problem to have, and we can absolutely help you avoid customer-facing errors. High-level proposal below; I'll loop in ops/finance for pricing and doc work.

1) Short-term uplift: we can provision a decoupled monthly commit increase for Dec and Jan only (convertible) — propose a 2.5x committed token band for Dec and a review on Jan 15. If you choose to keep the uplift, we can convert to a stepped multi-month commit with a 10% discount over listed hosted rates.

2) Throttle guard + fallback routing: implement a soft-throttle policy that routes overflow to a lower-cost quantized model variant or to a queued backfill path (best-effort) depending on latency sensitivity. We can enable prefix caching on your high-volume routes to reduce token burn immediately.

3) Timeline: We can standby-provision capacity within 24–48 hours once the workbook is accepted and billing is cleared. SLA addendum + quick DocuSign for immediate capacity.

I've attached a one-page workbook you can drop numbers into; Ben (cc) will share pricing and the SLA addendum draft.

Next step: if this aligns, please confirm quick acceptance and we’ll send a DocuSign for the temporary uplift.

—Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: FastStore_commit_workbook.xlsx (type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T08:22:00-05:00
Subject: FW: FastStore Q4 spike — need quick uplift (pricing + ops ask)

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Ari's note. TL;DR: Dec spike likely 2–3x; they asked for a short-term 2.5x commit with option to convert. They need (A) price for 2.5x for Dec+Jan, (B) SLA addendum for surge protection, and (C) an ops play to enable soft-throttle -> fallback routing and prefix caching as quick wins. Can you confirm: approved discount band for conversion, expected provisioning lead time, and whether we can enable fallback routing without an infra change? I want to deliver a single DocuSign package to the customer today.

Thanks — Laura
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T10:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: FW: FastStore Q4 spike — need quick uplift (pricing + ops ask)

Laura — confirmed we can do the temporary uplift + conversion path. Pricing: 2.5x hosted commit for Dec and Jan at a 7% uplift discount vs month-to-month list rates; conversion to a stepped 3-month commit gives a 10% blended discount. I'll attach the SLA addendum (PDF) for legal to review — it includes a soft-throttle / overflow routing clause and an explicit provisioning SLA: 24–48 hours provision window for reserve capacity.

Ops note: we can enable prefix caching and a routed fallback to a quantized variant on the same model family with feature-flagging — no infra migration required. Latency tradeoffs will be documented and we can pin critical routes to non-quantized variants if they exceed a latency threshold. Ops will need the workbook numbers to size the pool.

Attaching: proposed_sla_addendum.pdf.

—Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_sla_addendum.pdf (type: application/pdf)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Ari Shah <ari@faststore.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@faststore.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T16:22:00-05:00
Subject: FastStore — DocuSign & confirmed uplift plan for Dec+Jan

Hi Ari / Priya — thanks for the quick sync earlier. Summary and next steps below:

What we agreed:
- Temporary uplift: 2.5x hosted commit for Dec and Jan (Dec 1–Jan 31).
- Conversion option: review Jan 15 to convert to a stepped 3-month commit at a 10% discount.
- Throttle guard: soft-throttle enabled immediately; overflow routed to quantized model variant (best-effort). Critical routes pinned to non-quantized variant with prefix caching enabled.
- Provisioning SLA: standby capacity in 24–48 hours after signed acceptance.

Action items:
1) Ari/Priya: confirm acceptance in reply so I can send the DocuSign envelope.
2) FastStore: fill the attached workbook if you want exact capacity sizing (optional for initial uplift).
3) Redwood: Ben will kick off provisioning once DocuSign is complete.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-faststore-uplift
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DL-2026-0897

If you want the uplift to be prorated for Dec only, we can adjust — but given the campaign runway we recommend the two-month band to smooth provisioning.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
